meta: Cleopatra drops a priceless pearl into her wine at a banquet for Mark Antony, painted by Gerard Hoet.
about: Cleopatra sits under a canopy at the banquet she gives for Mark Antony and holds a glass of wine into which she is about to drop a priceless pearl earring, a show of indifference to wealth. The pearl dissolves, and she drinks the wine to Antony's health. In return he gives her Cyprus, Phoenicia, Coele-Syria and parts of Arabia. Gerard Hoet painted it in the late 1600s or early 1700s, and it is in the Getty.

meta: Saint Francis swoons into an angel's arms in Giovanni Baglione's Ecstasy of Saint Francis of 1601, his first Caravaggesque painting.
about: Saint Francis swoons into the arms of an angel after meditating on the instruments of Christ's torture, which another angel shows him at the left. The museum calls it Baglione's most accomplished painting and his first known Caravaggesque one, with realistic figures and dramatic lighting like Caravaggio's. That phase was brief. It ended after 1603, when Baglione took Caravaggio to court in a notorious trial, accusing him of slander for passing around malicious poems about him.

meta: Two elephants fight before the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah in Nainsukh's painting of about 1730 to 1740.
about: Muhammad Shah, who ruled from 1719 to 1748, watches two elephants fight in a courtyard from his window of public audience, marked by a golden carpet, smoking a hookah. Women of his harem look on from behind painted screens. Two pairs of men hold fire brands and spears to keep the elephants from running off, and one trainer has dropped his goad and is about to jump. Nainsukh came from a small Himalayan kingdom and painted scenes of his stay at the Delhi court.

meta: Colonel Josiah Parker, Virginia soldier and congressman, in a miniature by John Ramage, about 1780.
about: Josiah Parker was a Revolutionary soldier and politician who served in Virginia under George Washington, becoming a major in 1776 and a colonel the next year. He fought at Trenton, Princeton and Brandywine, but his short temper made him resign in 1778. He later served as a naval officer for Norfolk and in the First Congress, where he voted to put the Capitol on the Potomac. He wears his uniform here, though the miniature was probably painted when he took his seat in Congress.

meta: A birth tray by Masaccio of about 1423, the Berlin Tondo, showing a house a few days after a birth.
about: This birth tray, known as the Berlin Tondo, is a desco da parto painted by Masaccio around 1423, a short time after his San Giovenale Triptych of 1422. With its frame it is 66 centimeters across. The top side shows a scene probably a few days after a child's birth, on the ground floor of a well-to-do house with white and black stone facings, in a very modern style for Tuscan architecture. An arcade of round arches leads to a garden.

meta: A boy meets a holy hermit in Mikhail Nesterov's The Vision to the Youth Bartholomew, painted in 1889 to 1890.
about: Mikhail Nesterov painted this picture in 1889 and 1890 as the first of his series on Sergius of Radonezh, a medieval Russian saint who was born Bartholomew. Wikipedia calls it the inaugural work of Russian Symbolism. Nesterov had loved the image of Sergius since childhood, seeing in him a moral ideal, and gave him an important role in rallying the Russian people. The painting is in the Tretyakov Gallery in Moscow.

meta: A full-immersion baptism in a water tank under a raven and a dove in John Steuart Curry's Baptism in Kansas, 1928.
about: A full-immersion baptism takes place in a water tank, with a raven and a dove in the sky, recalling the birds Noah released from the ark. Curry based it on a scene he saw in 1915, when the creeks were dry and the tank was the only place to baptize. He painted it in August 1928. Gertrude Vanderbilt Whitney bought it in 1930, and it has belonged to the Whitney Museum since its opening in 1931.

meta: Pinturicchio's Saint Jerome in the Desert of about 1475 to 1480, bought by Henry Walters in 1916.
about: Pinturicchio painted this Saint Jerome in the desert around 1475 to 1480, one of the earliest dated works given to him, just after his work on the Miracles of Saint Bernardino. It belonged to the Bartoccini family in Perugia and then to the Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria, until it was sold in 1915. Henry Walters bought it in 1916 on Bernard Berenson's advice. It formed part of the original core of the Walters Art Museum in 1931 and was restored in 1966.

meta: A ferry lands two wealthy women while cattle rest in Alvan Fisher's early landscape of 1816.
about: A ferry delivers two wealthy women and their belongings ashore while a herd of especially handsome cattle rests in the foreground. The museum calls this a prime example of Alvan Fisher's early rural pictures. Fisher, based in Boston, was among the first American artists to specialize in landscape, and he recalled that this novel kind of painting was more lucrative, pleasant and distinguishing than portraits.
credit_line: Mr. and Mrs. William H. Marlatt Fund

meta: Designs for painted panels with a candelabrum, the wheel of fortune and a blindfolded woman, by Claude-Louis Desrais, about 1780.
about: A candelabrum with two half figures carries a vase on which a fantastic bearded animal rests. Snakes growing from his head hold a censer with two putti on it. Two cornucopias come out of the wheel of fortune with terrible and marvelous gifts. At the top a blindfolded nude woman with coins and a banner stands beneath a military trophy. Claude-Louis Desrais made the designs around 1780.

meta: Eleven-year-old Elizabeth Spiegel with a recorder, representing hearing in Dirck Dircksz. Santvoort's portrait of 1639.
about: This portrait of 11-year-old Elizabeth Spiegel, who holds a recorder, stands for the sense of hearing. It belongs to a series of portraits of the five senses, each showing a daughter of a wealthy Amsterdam family. Her costly satin gown and pearl ornaments proclaim her family's wealth, and the ostrich feathers imported from Africa point to Amsterdam's role as a center of world trade. Dirck Dircksz. Santvoort painted it in 1639.
credit_line: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Noah L. Butkin

meta: Maria Kitscher, wife of a Bavarian court family, in Hans Mielich's portrait of 1545 with a ring that hides a message.
about: Maria von Freyberg belonged to the court of Albert V, Duke of Bavaria, but as Lutherans her family eventually lost favor when Catholic interests took power. Hans Mielich also illustrated an inventory of the duchess's jewelry, and the same close attention shows in the sitter's brooches, necklaces and rings. The museum says the diamond and ruby ring on her left index finger would have slid apart to reveal a private message or image underneath. Mielich painted it in 1545.
